prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from airport acceptance/transfer induction through screening, sorting, reconciliation, staging and aircraft-loading handoff; excludes loading beyond outbound load control point.
Elements/functions:
Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records accepted bags, initiates processing, sends Oversize Exception Ticket.
Bag Tag Printer produces durable uniquely identified tags; identifiers associate passenger/flight records in Baggage Control System (Velvet).
Velvet coordinates status/routing/visibility using current flight/operating data; checks flight acceptance open, records complete, and transfer data against routing before induction.
Transfer Bag Feeder identifies/records inbound bags; sends Late Transfer Bag Card.
Flight Data Gateway supplies flight/routing records; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory.
Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates local conveyance/equipment; produces Recovery Route Card; grants induction permissive only when equipment status/restrictions allow movement.
Induction Tray Conveyor accepts controlled feeds, separates successive bags.
Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes cleared bags to make-up.
North Gate Scanner; South Gate Scanner: screening interfaces.
Image Resolution Desk: operator image review.
Secondary Inspection Chute: additional examination path.
Explosives Response Team; Security Duty Manager: escalated security response/disposition.
Bag Reconciliation Station: identity/status verification.
East Make-Up Conveyor; West Make-Up Conveyor: convey toward loading.
Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit: departure staging.
Outbound Load Control Desk: handoff readiness confirmation.
Airline Ramp Coordinator: ramp acceptance.
Baggage Operations Supervisor oversees flow/interruption recovery with Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician.
Requirements: staff confirm airline eligibility, passenger/flight details before acceptance; check dimensions/weight against configured conveyor limits. Missing/unreadable/conflicting acceptance data held for staff resolution; oversized bags held pending approved route. Staff verify legible transfer identifiers/valid onward flight. Before induction: valid record, available route, ready receiving equipment. Defined interfaces exchange equipment status, bag identity, routing state, restrictions; local staff resolve automation-uncleared conditions.
Objectives: safe screening, accurate bag-flight association, predictable throughput, departure-cutoff delivery.
No explicit modes; ticket/card/advisory recipients unspecified.

New part:
S045: Interlocks stop feed movement when a jam, access-door opening, or loss of downstream readiness is detected.
S046: The North Gate Scanner reads the bag identifier as the bag enters the screening and sorting network.
S047: The North Gate Scanner is also known locally as Kestrel.
S048: The South Gate Scanner provides an independent read point for bags routed through its assigned entry path.
S049: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter receives inducted bags and directs them according to the active routing data.
S050: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is also known locally as Juniper.
S051: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S052: The Airline Ramp Coordinator sends a Carousel Release Slip when the outbound build is authorized.
S053: The Baggage Control System applies the approved screening profile to each bag using its tag data and the current operating configuration.
S054: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags to the screening equipment at a controlled spacing that supports reliable image capture.
S055: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter maintains bag identity and routes each bag according to the screening disposition available at the time of sorting.
S056: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner acquire screening images and return a disposition for each bag that passes through them.
S057: Screening equipment records image quality and alarm status so that an incomplete examination is not treated as a clear result.
S058: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S059: The reviewer considers the full image, bag identification, and any system prompts before assigning a disposition.
S060: A bag remains under controlled routing while its image is awaiting review, and the system prevents it from entering an outbound make-up path prematurely.
S061: The South Gate Scanner produces a Manual Rescan Receipt when a manual rescan is required.
S062: A clear disposition permits normal routing only when the bag identity and screening record agree.
S063: An alarm, an unresolved image, or a missing screening record places the bag into an exception status for additional examination.
S064: The Baggage Control System routes exception-status bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute through a path that avoids normal outbound flows.
S065: The chute is monitored for occupancy so that a bag is not released into a blocked or unavailable inspection position.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response:
